correctness.rationale: Starting from actual scalar scaled ADMM update, inactive threshold input r^j=(b/rho)(1-(1+rho)^(-j)). Strict inequality b(1-(1+rho)^(-j))>lambda yields exact first positive index floor(log(b/(b-lambda))/log(1+rho))+1, including equality case. At activation scaled dual u=lambda/rho and 0<z<b-lambda. Subsequent recurrence z_next=(b-lambda+rho*z)/(1+rho) has never-vanishing geometric error factor rho/(1+rho), any finite rho>0. Active-cell Jacobian has eigenvalues rho/(1+rho),0. Independently replayed exact fractions for five choices (b,lambda,rho), including b=2,lambda=rho=1 giving j=2,z^2=1/2; the all-parameter result follows from the recurrence, not tests.

value.rationale: A minimal, hypothesis-faithful scalar counterexample invalidates a specific published claim that K=I anisotropic ADMM reaches a fixed point finitely. It preserves the established finite support-identification theorem while exposing the precise opposing penalty tradeoff: faster identification for larger rho, slower post-identification contraction.

limitations: Only scalar b>lambda>0, finite fixed rho>0 and initialized z0=u0=0, standard unrelaxed scaled ADMM.
Finite computer replay cannot by itself prove infinite nontermination.
An unindexed erratum or earlier scalar ADMM note may observe the same particular counterexample.
No claim on arbitrary initialization, penalty schedules or multivariate designs.
